_note: the Mouse and the Dormouse share a file, in this order, on purpose. The GT loader binds a page to the first entity whose alias matches by bidirectional substring, and the page title 'Mouse' is a substring of the alias 'Dormouse'. Listing the Mouse first makes 'Mouse' bind to the Mouse and 'Dormouse' bind to the Dormouse; splitting them across files leaves the binding to glob order. A string value here is skipped by the loader, which only reads dict values.

known_facts_book1: Is swimming in the pool of Alice's tears when she meets it — the first creature she speaks to in Wonderland.
Alice addresses it with 'O Mouse!', remembering her brother's Latin Grammar, then in French with 'Où est ma chatte?', which terrifies it.
Says 'Our family always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things!' and asks 'Would you like cats if you were me?'
Is offended a second time when Alice praises a farmer's terrier for catching mice.
Leads the swimming party to the shore and calls the meeting to order.
Recites the driest thing it knows — the passage about William the Conqueror and Stigand, archbishop of Canterbury — to dry the party out.
Says 'Mine is a long and a sad tale!', which Alice takes for a long tail, and the tale is printed in the shape of one.
Walks off offended in the middle of its own story and does not come back.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Offended by her twice, over cats and then over dogs; leaves the beach rather than finish its history.
known_relations_book1.Dodo: Fellow member of the draggled party on the bank; the Dodo proposes the Caucus-race after the Mouse's history fails to dry anyone.
known_relations_book1.Lory: Part of the same party; interrupts the Mouse's recitation.
known_relations_book1.Dinah: Never meets her — Alice's talk about Dinah is what frightens and offends it.

not_in_this_book: the Mouse reappears after chapter III

hallucination_signals: the Mouse falls asleep at the tea party

known_facts_book1: Sits between the Hatter and the March Hare, fast asleep, and the other two use it as a cushion.
Talks in its sleep and is pinched and shaken awake.
Tells the story of three little sisters — Elsie, Lacie and Tillie — who lived at the bottom of a treacle-well.
Says the sisters were learning to draw things that begin with an M — mouse-traps, the moon, memory, muchness.
Falls asleep mid-story; the last Alice sees of the party is the other two trying to put it into the teapot.
Comes into the court arm-in-arm with the March Hare; when the Hatter says the tea party began on the fourteenth of March and the March Hare says the fifteenth, the Dormouse says the sixteenth.
Says 'Treacle' in a sleepy voice from behind the cook, and the Queen shrieks 'Collar that Dormouse! Behead that Dormouse! Turn that Dormouse out of court!'

known_relations_book1.Hatter: Is woken, pinched and doused with hot tea by him.
known_relations_book1.March Hare: Is used as a cushion and finally stuffed toward the teapot by him.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Its story is interrupted by her questions, which the other two treat as rudeness.
